title: Beef Pad Krapow
subtitle: Thai holy basil beef. 6 min prep, 8 min cook.

ingredients.thai_market_tip: Ask the Tops/Villa butcher to mince a lean sirloin steak. Hand-chopped beats supermarket mince for texture.

ingredients.note: One per serving, fried hard with crispy edges.
Oil cap — split: half for the beef, half for the eggs.
Pound with the chilies — don't fine-mince.

ingredients.item: Thai bird's eye chili (prik kee noo)

ingredients.thai_market_tip: Maekrua or Lee Kum Kee. Maekrua is the local default.
Healthy Boy brand. The brown-lacquer maker.
MUST be holy basil (bai krapow), not horapha. Fresh-market only.

substitutions.note: More forgiving at high heat. Lower fat. Cook 1 min less.

steps.text: Pound garlic + chilies in mortar to rough paste.
Heat 1/2 tsp oil in non-stick wok, high. Add paste, 15 sec until fragrant.
Add minced beef. Press flat 30 sec to brown, then stir-fry until no pink, ~4 min.
Add oyster sauce, fish sauce, dark soy, sugar, stock. Toss 1 min until glossy.
Kill heat. Throw in holy basil, toss twice — leaves wilt from residual heat.
Plate. Wipe pan, add remaining 1/2 tsp oil, fry eggs hard. Slide one onto each plate.

notes: Same skeleton as pad krapow gai — different beast. Lean sirloin browns better than thigh and gives more umami. Holy basil non-negotiable; horapha is the wrong dish. Fried egg with runny yolk is the sauce.
